# Business Automation and Custom Software FAQ 2027
URL: https://www.groviadigi.in/faq/

Questions

## Good to know before we talk.

What does Groviadigi do? We build custom CRMs, automations, internal tools and websites. The goal is simple: stop your team doing the same manual work again and again, like copying data between sheets, chasing follow-ups or making reports by hand.

Why is the consultancy paid, and what if I go ahead? The consultancy is real work: we meet your team, map how the work is done, check the tools you already use and write a plan with costs. If the free call shows you do not need software or automation, we tell you and stop there, with nothing to pay. If you decide to go ahead, the consultancy fee is included in your project fee, so you do not pay twice. Your software goes live only after you approve it.

Does my business need automation or custom software? Not always. We look at your process first. Sometimes a small change is enough. Sometimes only a few steps need automating. Sometimes the whole process can run by itself. You get an honest answer on the first call.

How long does a custom CRM or automation project take? A small automation can be ready in a few days. A custom CRM, internal tool or website usually takes 3 to 8 weeks. You get a written plan, timeline and price before any work starts.

How much does custom software or automation cost? Prices depend on the project, so we do not publish a price list. After the free call and the consultancy, you get a fixed written quote before the build starts. Every project includes 3 months of free maintenance, and care plans after that start at ₹5,000 a month.

Can you work with the tools we already use? Yes. We work with what you already use, like Google Sheets, WhatsApp, email, forms and your current CRM. You don’t have to replace everything.

What happens after launch? We launch it, train your team and give you simple guides. Every project includes 3 months of free maintenance for fixes and support. After that, you can choose a monthly care plan from ₹5,000 for fixes, updates and improvements.

Zapier vs custom code automation: which is cheaper? If it runs often, custom code is usually cheaper over time. Zapier, Make and n8n charge a monthly fee that goes up the more you use them. We write the automation in code, so you pay once to build it, then only a small hosting cost.

Is my data safe with your automations? We build for that. Your data goes straight between your own apps, not through another company’s platform. Access keys are stored securely, each automation only gets the access it needs, the code stays in your account, and we can sign an NDA before we see any of your data.

Custom CRM or Zoho / HubSpot: which is better for a small business? If a standard CRM fits how you sell, use it; we can set it up for you. A custom CRM makes sense when you keep working around your software, pay for users you don’t need, or need steps like site visits, quotes or part payments built in.

Do you work with businesses outside India? Yes. We work with businesses in India, US and UAE, and schedule calls in your time zone.

# Solar CRM Case Study: Conversion Up 28% | Groviadigi
URL: https://www.groviadigi.in/work/solar-crm-smart-sun-power/

← All work · Case study 

Solar CRM · Smart Sun Power

## A custom CRM for a rooftop solar installer

Lead management, site surveys, quotations, installations and payments, brought into one platform for Smart Sun Power.

Client Smart Sun Power 
Industry Rooftop solar installation 
Segments Residential and commercial 
Engagement Custom solar CRM 

+28% lead conversion within 3 months 
38% faster sales cycle: 45 to 28 days 
35% better on-time collections 
30% less admin overhead 

## Executive summary
Before the CRM, Smart Sun Power ran its whole sales and project pipeline across WhatsApp chats, phone calls, spreadsheets and scattered files. Follow-ups were missed, quotations went untracked and management had little visibility. The custom solar CRM brings lead management, follow-ups, site surveys, quotations, installation tracking and payments into one connected platform, so the business sees its whole pipeline in real time.

## The challenge

Fragmented lead management Leads arrived through WhatsApp, calls and the website, with no single place to see them. 
Missed follow-ups With no task list or reminders, follow-ups depended on memory and some leads went cold. 
Disorganised documents Survey notes, quotations and customer files were spread across chats, email and folders. 
No tracking after the sale Once a deal closed, nobody could see where procurement, installation and commissioning stood. 
Low management visibility Pipeline value, conversion and payments were hard to see without asking around. 

## What we built

01 Lead management dashboard Leads from the website, calls and WhatsApp referrals land in one place, each with a sales owner and a tracked source. 
02 Automated follow-ups The team logs calls and sets next actions; the system alerts them the moment a follow-up is due. 
03 Site surveys and quotations Surveys move from scheduled to completed; quotation templates fill in lead and site data and go from draft to final. 
04 Installation tracking Closed deals move straight into installation, with milestones from material procurement to commissioning. 
05 Payments and collections Advance, on-installation and on-completion milestones with due dates, alerts and linked receipts. 
06 Executive dashboard Pipeline value, conversion, sales-cycle length, team performance, profitability and payment status in real time. 

## How it works

Lead captured
Sales owner assigned
Site survey
Quotation
Installation
Payments

## What changed

Area Before the CRM After go-live 
Leads WhatsApp chats, calls and spreadsheets One dashboard, each lead with an owner and a source 
Follow-ups Dependent on memory Reminders the moment one is due 
Projects No view after the sale Milestones from procurement to commissioning 
Payments Overdue amounts hard to spot Milestones with due dates and alerts 
Sales cycle 45 days from enquiry to close 28 days from enquiry to close 

“What used to take three people to coordinate manually is now automated. Our team is more organised, our leads are never lost, and our owner has full visibility into the business.” Smart Sun Power, management team 

## How we delivered it

Discovery Interviews with the sales team, operations manager and owner. 
Custom development Built around their solar process, not a generic CRM template. 
Data migration Existing leads and customer records moved in, nothing lost. 
Team training Hands-on onboarding, documentation and quick-reference guides. 
Ongoing support Fixes, updates and new features based on real use. 

## Why it worked

Built around solar work Surveys, quotations, installation milestones and payment stages match how an installer works. 
Nothing lost in the switch Leads and customer records were migrated before the team moved over. 
A team that uses it Training and support made the CRM the daily tool, not a side project.

# How to Merge Duplicate Leads From Spreadsheets (2027)
URL: https://www.groviadigi.in/blog/merge-duplicate-leads-master-list/

← Blog · Data tools 

## How to merge duplicate leads from multiple spreadsheets into one master list

Contact lists arrived from Apollo, past campaigns and the ad platforms, and the same person could sit in three of them. Here is the master list we built for a cross-border CFO firm, and what a spreadsheet can and cannot do on its own.

AT 
Abhuday Tripathi Founder, Groviadigi · 16 November 2026 

7 min read 

Short answer Put every list into the same columns, clean the field you match on (usually the email address), and keep one record per person in a single master list. Check each new file against that master before anything is added, and mark contacts as used the moment you export them to a channel. A spreadsheet can handle the first part; once lists arrive every week from several tools, a small custom tool like the Data Sorter we built for a cross-border CFO firm keeps the checks and the usage record in one place.

## Why duplicate leads cost more than they look

The client is a cross-border finance firm. It runs cold email and paid campaigns on Meta and LinkedIn from the same pool of contacts. Those contacts came from three places: Apollo exports, past campaigns re-enriched in Clay, and data from the Meta and LinkedIn ad platforms. Each arrived as its own file.

The same person could sit in two or three of those files at once. Every copy cost something. It might be a sending slot, an export credit, or ad budget spent showing the same message to the same founder twice. And with no usage record, a channel could contact someone it had already used.

None of this is unusual. Most teams that buy or build lists end up with one spreadsheet per source and a habit of comparing them by hand. That is fine at a few hundred rows. It stops being fine when the outbound plan targets 10,000 to 15,000 emails a month to roughly 3,000 to 4,000 people, across eight audience segments that each need fresh contacts. That was the programme Data Sorter was built to support.

The numbers Data Sorter works with, taken from the signed case study. 

## How to merge duplicate leads from multiple spreadsheets

If you only have a handful of files, you do not need software. A spreadsheet will do, as long as you follow the same steps every time.

Use the same columns everywhere. Before merging, make every list match one layout: name, email, company, country, source, date added. Exports from different tools label the same field differently, so map them first.

Clean the field you match on. Trim spaces and put emails in lower case. Under the email standard, RFC 5321 , the domain part is not case-sensitive. The part before the @ technically can be, but in practice two addresses that differ only in case almost always reach the same person, so most teams treat them as one.

Pick one match key and stick to it. Email is the usual choice. Name plus company is a weaker fallback, because people change jobs and spell their names in different ways.

Stack the lists and remove duplicates. Paste everything into one sheet with a column for the source, then keep one row per email. In Google Sheets the UNIQUE function returns the distinct rows; Excel has a Remove Duplicates button that does the same job.

Add a status column. Fresh or used, and which channel used them. Without this, the merge is clean today and messy again next week.

Step five is where spreadsheets struggle. Removing duplicates tells you nothing about history. Someone has to remember to update the status after every export, and the day they forget is the day a contact gets the same pitch twice.

## What we built for the firm

We built Data Sorter, an internal tool with six screens, each doing one job. We started by mapping every source of contacts and every channel that uses them. Then we defined one master record per contact, with a usage status and a history of exports. Only after that did we build the screens.

## Upload and Compare: two checks before anything is added

Nothing joins the master list unchecked. 
Every new list is checked against the master database. Two checks run on every upload: is this contact already in the master, and has this contact already been used? Both are flagged before anything is added, so the team decides what to do with them instead of finding out after a campaign has gone out.

## Master Data: one list in place of a spreadsheet per source

All contacts live in one searchable list with filters. The marketing team no longer opens four files to answer one question. Every channel draws from the same list, so everyone sees the same counts and statuses.

## Segments built with filters

Audiences are built with filters for country, industry and usage status. A campaign for founders in one country starts from relevant, unused contacts rather than from several files joined by hand.

## Export by channel, with a usage rule

Data Sorter exports for four channels: outbound email, Meta Ads, LinkedIn Ads and newsletters. When contacts are exported to a channel, they are marked as used at that moment. The next audience for that channel can filter them out, which helps avoid pitching the same person twice.

## Dashboard, history and backup

The dashboard shows total records, fresh and used contacts, channel usage and audience breakdowns, such as founders by country, on one screen. Every upload and export is logged with its date, so the team can see which list came from where and what went to each channel. There is a settings page and a backup option.

How a list moves through Data Sorter. The checks happen before the master list, not after the campaign. 

## Why the usage record matters as much as the merge

Most advice about duplicate leads stops at removing them. In this project the harder problem was repeat contact across channels. A person can be unique in the master list and still be emailed in March and shown a LinkedIn ad with the same offer in April, simply because nobody wrote down the first contact.

This matters for sending too. Mailbox providers watch how people react to your mail. Google’s email sender guidelines ask senders to keep spam complaints low and to send only to people who want the mail. Emailing the same person repeatedly from different lists is an easy way to collect complaints you did not need.

Credits were the other reason. Apollo export credits are limited and may run as an annual pool, so past campaign contacts had value. Data Sorter lets the team re-check and reuse them with care, instead of buying the same people again.

The same work, before and after one master database. 

## What we learned building it

Decide what counts as one person before writing any code. The record design came before the screens. If the match rule is vague, no amount of software fixes it.

Record usage at export, not later by hand. The moment a file leaves for a channel is the only moment you can be sure what was sent. Anything that relies on someone updating a column afterwards will drift.

Keep history, even when it feels unnecessary. The upload and export log is the least exciting screen. It is also the one that answers “where did this contact come from?” when something goes wrong.

Not every team needs this. If you add one or two lists a month and use a single channel, a well-kept spreadsheet with a status column is enough. We would tell you that on the first call. A tool like Data Sorter earns its place when lists arrive from several tools, several channels draw from them, and credits or ad budget are limited.

## Could this work for your team?

If your team pulls lists from more than one tool and worries about duplicates or contacting people twice, the answer is probably yes. We build tools like this in code, around your own data and the channels you already use. You can read the full Data Sorter case study, see how it feeds the outbound automation connected to Zoho CRM, look at our services , or read how the same client automated SEO without losing human review . When you are ready, tell us about your lists .

## Frequently asked questions
How do I merge duplicate leads from multiple spreadsheets? Put every list into the same columns, add a column for the source, clean the email field (trim spaces, lower case), stack the lists in one sheet and keep one row per email. In Google Sheets the UNIQUE function does this; Excel has a Remove Duplicates button. Add a status column so you know who has already been contacted.
What is the best field to match duplicate contacts on? Email address is the most reliable key, once it is trimmed and put in lower case. Name plus company can work as a fallback, but it misses people who changed jobs or spell their names differently.
Can Excel or Google Sheets remove duplicate leads automatically? They can remove duplicates inside one sheet when you run the command or formula. They do not check new files against your history on their own, and they do not record which channel has already used a contact. That part needs a process or a small tool.
When do I need a lead deduplication tool instead of a spreadsheet? When lists arrive regularly from several tools, more than one channel draws from them, and repeat contact or wasted credits start to cost you. If you add one or two lists a month for one channel, a spreadsheet with a status column is usually enough.
How much does a custom master contact list tool cost? It depends on how many sources and channels it connects. Groviadigi gives a fixed written quote after a free 15-minute call and a short consultancy to map your data. If the call shows a spreadsheet will do, we say so and stop there.

Groviadigi

# SEO Automation With Human Review: 2027 Guide
URL: https://www.groviadigi.in/blog/seo-automation-with-human-review/

← Blog · SEO automation 

## How we automated SEO for a finance firm without losing the human review

One dashboard now plans the month, researches, writes and fact-checks. A person still decides what gets published. Here is what we built for a cross-border CFO firm, and what we learned.

AT 
Abhuday Tripathi Founder, Groviadigi · 15 November 2026 

8 min read 

Short answer We built Growth Center, an SEO dashboard for a cross-border CFO firm, because no single tool covered the whole job. It pulls real data from Google Search Console, Analytics and a rank tracker, plans a 30-day strategy, writes each blog with research, fact-checks it against official sources with two AI models, and gives the team 48 hours to approve, reject, pause or reschedule it. The machine does the repetitive work. People keep the final say.

## Why SEO by hand stopped working

The client is a cross-border finance firm. Its readers are founders, NRIs and finance professionals, and plenty of them will spot a wrong tax rate in the first paragraph. So every blog needs research, every figure needs a source, and every rule needs to be current. That makes SEO slow.

Before Growth Center, the work lived in spreadsheets: a keyword tool in one tab, Google Search Console in another, and a writer waiting on both. None of it was hard. It was scattered. Most of the week went into moving information from one place to another.

So we asked a simple question: what if one dashboard held the plan, the data, the writing and the review, and only called a person when a real decision was needed?

The monthly loop. One human decision at the start steers everything after it. 

## What Growth Center does

## 1. It plans the month from real data

Every month the dashboard collects numbers from each connected tool: clicks and impressions from Search Console, traffic from Google Analytics, rankings and AI visibility from the rank tracker, and the questions clients asked in meetings. From that it drafts a 30-day plan covering keywords, a blog calendar, AEO and GEO targets, backlinks and technical fixes.

Two rules keep the plan honest. It may only use numbers from the data it was given, and every target must beat last month’s actual result. When a number is missing, the plan says DATA MISSING instead of guessing.

## 2. One goal, three pillars: SEO, AEO and GEO

We gave the whole system one goal: grow client conversions through blogs, SEO, AEO and GEO. Every keyword and every blog in the plan names the pillar it serves.

Rankings matter because they lead to clients. Writing that down changed how topics get picked. 
If you are new to the terms: SEO gets a page ranked on Google, AEO (answer engine optimisation) gets it picked as the direct answer in snippets and voice results, and GEO (generative engine optimisation) gets the firm named when someone asks ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity. Buyers now move between all three, so the dashboard reports on each one separately.

## 3. It writes and fact-checks each blog

Nothing goes out unverified. 
About 72 hours before a blog’s slot, the dashboard researches the topic: the pages ranking now in the US and India, Google’s “People also ask” questions, and primary sources such as the IRS, CBDT and RBI. Then it writes the draft in the firm’s house voice, with a direct answer at the top, an FAQ and one clear call to action.

Before anyone on the team sees it, the draft is checked against official sources. Two different AI models check it in turn, and a blog that cannot be fully verified is never published. A plagiarism check runs as well.

This matters more in finance than almost anywhere else. A confident paragraph with an outdated deadline does real damage to trust, and no amount of traffic makes up for that.

## 4. People review, and the dashboard waits for them

This is the part we refused to automate away. Each blog opens a 48-hour review. The team can approve it, reject it with feedback (the dashboard rewrites it and shows what changed), pause it, or move it to another day. When someone reschedules, the dashboard suggests free days that still leave time for writing and review.

The review queue. Tax and compliance posts wait for a named CA or CPA. 
Tax, legal and compliance blogs never publish on their own. They wait for a named CA or CPA reviewer.

## 5. It learns from the team’s edits

Every edit a reviewer makes is recorded: how much of the text changed, which sentences, whether a number or a heading moved. Once a day those edits become lessons for the writer, so the next draft needs less fixing. If someone uploads a blog they wrote themselves, the dashboard can optimise it for search and AI answers while keeping their sentences and facts.

## 6. It does the follow-up nobody enjoys

After a blog goes live, the dashboard submits the page through IndexNow , resubmits the sitemap , adds the keyword to rank tracking and links the new post from older related posts. Every morning it also scans the last 24 hours of tax and compliance news, so the team knows what is worth writing about today.

## What we learned building it

Automate the steps, not the judgement. The dashboard is fast at research, drafting and checking. It is the wrong place to decide whether a sensitive tax post is ready for clients. That stays with people.

Make every number traceable. Each metric in the plan carries its source and date. A plan that guesses is worse than a plan that admits a gap.

Plan for pauses. AI work costs money. A paused or restarted job picks up from its saved steps, so nothing is paid for twice.

Respect what Google actually rewards. Google’s own guidance says it looks for helpful, reliable, people-first content , and that it judges content on its quality, not on how it was produced . Volume without review is what gets sites into trouble, so the review step is the core of the system, not an extra.

## Could this work for your business?

If you publish regularly and the work is scattered across tools, probably yes. The setup does not have to be this big. Many teams start with one piece, such as daily topic research or a review queue, and add the rest later. You can read the full project in our Growth Center case study, see the other services we offer , or read how the same team automated on-brand social media creatives .

## Frequently asked questions
Can SEO be fully automated? The repetitive parts can: data collection, research, drafting, checks and post-publish tasks. Deciding what matters to your clients and approving sensitive content still needs people, especially in finance, health and legal topics.
Does Google penalise AI-written content? Google says it rewards helpful content however it is made. The risk comes from publishing large volumes of unreviewed pages. A human review step and fact checks against primary sources address that.
What is the difference between SEO, AEO and GEO? SEO gets your pages ranked in Google and Bing. AEO gets your content picked as the direct answer in snippets, People also ask boxes and voice assistants. GEO gets your business named and cited when people ask AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity.
How long does SEO automation take to show results? New pages usually take days to weeks to be indexed, and competitive keywords can take months. Automation speeds up the work; it does not shortcut how search engines rank pages.
How much does an SEO automation dashboard cost to build? It depends on how many tools it connects and how much of the workflow it covers. Groviadigi gives a fixed written quote after a free 15-minute call and a short consultancy to map your process. Smaller pieces, such as daily topic research or a review queue, can be built first.

## A social media dashboard that designs, learns and keeps the brand consistent

How we built a social media dashboard that makes on-brand banners for every blog, learns design from videos the team picks, remembers its mistakes and works with an SEO dashboard.

# Social Media Automation That Stays On Brand (2027)
URL: https://www.groviadigi.in/blog/social-media-dashboard-brand-consistency/

← Blog · Social media automation 

## A social media dashboard that designs, learns and keeps the brand consistent

Every blog needed a banner and every update needed a post. Here is how we automated the creatives for a cross-border CFO firm without letting the brand drift.

AT 
Abhuday Tripathi Founder, Groviadigi · 14 November 2026 

7 min read 

Short answer The social media dashboard we built for a cross-border CFO firm turns each blog and update into on-brand creatives, so a designer doesn’t start from scratch every time. It follows one fixed brand kit, learns design techniques from videos the team picks, remembers what went wrong before, and shares what it learns with the firm’s SEO dashboard. A person still reviews what goes out.

## The problem: good content, inconsistent creatives

Once the SEO dashboard started producing blogs on a steady schedule, a new bottleneck showed up. Every blog needed a banner, every update needed a post, and every post had to look like it came from the same firm.

Designing each one by hand slowed everything down. And on busy weeks, when people rushed, the look drifted: a different font here, a slightly different blue there, a layout nobody had agreed on. Small things, but together they make a brand look careless.

The brief was short: creatives that are fast to make and always on brand.

## What the dashboard does

## 1. One brand, defined once

We started with the brand itself. The dashboard explored several colour directions, critiqued them and refined one. It worked out contrast and shades in code, so text stays readable on every background (the same idea behind the WCAG contrast guidelines ).

The fixed brand kit. Crimson is kept for small accents only. 
The result is a fixed kit: petrol navy, steel blue and soft teal as the main colours, a crimson used only for small accents, and two set typefaces. Every banner uses it. Nobody has to remember a hex code again.

## 2. A banner for every blog, automatically

No blog waits for its image. 
When a blog is planned in the SEO dashboard, the social dashboard makes its banner in the house design, with the title, the author’s name and a picture chosen for the topic. A light AI step picks better photo searches and decides which words of the title to highlight.

If the design service is down, the banner is still made with a simpler fallback layout. A blog never waits for its image, which sounds minor until a launch is held up by one missing banner.

## 3. It learns design from video

The team picks design and creative videos they like, and the dashboard watches them with an AI model that can read video. It takes notes, groups them by topic and turns them into creative skills: how to frame a title, how to use space, how to choose a picture. A master skill sums them up, and the banner and post steps follow it.

The dashboard gets better when the team finds a good example, without anyone rewriting prompts. 

## 4. Agents with memory

Different jobs run as different agents, and each keeps a memory of mistakes, lessons, team rules and incidents. When an agent gets something wrong and is corrected, the correction is remembered, and a mistake that keeps coming back gets more weight. An operations agent runs a daily health check and tracks each issue until it is fixed.

## 5. It talks to the SEO dashboard

The two dashboards share what they learn through a signed, read-only link. The SEO dashboard asks for the banner design and the design skills; the social dashboard reads the blog plan and the topics. Each side runs on its own, so if one is down, the other keeps working.

Two systems, one link, no single point of failure. 

## What we learned building it

Fix the brand before you automate it. Automation repeats whatever you give it, including the mess. A clear brand kit made every later step simpler.

Always have a fallback. Creative tools and APIs change. When one image model was retired, banners kept coming because the dashboard falls back to another route instead of failing.

Let the team teach it. The best improvements came from people pointing at a good example, not from engineers tuning settings.

Keep a person on the final step. The dashboard prepares creatives quickly, but a person still decides what goes out under the firm’s name. That is the same rule we follow in Growth Center and in every automation we build.

## Is social media automation right for you?

If you post often and your designer spends most of the week resizing titles, it is worth a look. Start by writing down your brand rules; that alone fixes much of the drift. Then automate the repeatable formats first, such as blog banners, quote cards and announcements. You can see what else we build in our services section, or tell us about your content workflow .

## Frequently asked questions
Can social media creatives be automated without losing brand consistency? Yes, if the brand is defined first. A fixed palette, set fonts and a house layout give the automation clear rules, so every creative looks like it belongs to the same company.
Does AI-made design replace a designer? Not fully. It handles the repetitive banners and posts, so designers and marketers spend their time on campaigns and new ideas instead of resizing titles. A person should still approve what goes out.
How does a social media dashboard work with SEO? Each blog the SEO dashboard plans gets its banner from the social dashboard, and both share what they learn, so search content and social content stay in step.
What happens if an AI image tool stops working? A good setup always has a fallback. In this dashboard, if the design service or an image model is unavailable, the banner is still made with a simpler layout, so nothing waits.
How long does it take to build a social media automation dashboard? A first version that makes on-brand banners for one format can go live in a few weeks. Learning from video, agent memory and links to other systems are added in stages. Groviadigi quotes a fixed price after a free call and a short consultancy to map your process.

# Custom CRM for Small Business in 2027: A 3-Month Result
URL: https://www.groviadigi.in/blog/whatsapp-to-custom-solar-crm/

← Blog · Custom CRM 

## From WhatsApp chats to a custom solar CRM: what changed in 3 months

Leads came in on WhatsApp, follow-ups lived in people’s heads and nobody could see a project once the deal closed. Here is the CRM we built for a rooftop solar installer, the numbers after three months, and the honest lessons.

AT 
Abhuday Tripathi Founder, Groviadigi · 26 November 2026 

8 min read 

Short answer We moved Smart Sun Power, a rooftop solar installer, off WhatsApp chats, phone calls and spreadsheets and onto one custom CRM that covers leads, follow-ups, site surveys, quotations, installation and payments. Within three months lead conversion rose 28%, the sales cycle fell from 45 to 28 days, on-time collections improved by 35% and admin overhead dropped by 30%. The gains came from three plain things: every lead has an owner, every follow-up has a reminder, and every project is visible after the sale.

## What changed in three months

The short version: the business stopped losing track of things. Before the CRM, Smart Sun Power’s whole pipeline sat in WhatsApp chats, phone calls, spreadsheets and folders. Three months after go-live, the numbers looked like this.

The first three months after go-live, from the signed case study. 
None of these came from clever technology. They came from making the basics impossible to forget. A lead that arrives on WhatsApp now gets an owner. A promised call-back now has a date and an alert. A signed customer now has an installation record that the owner can open without phoning anyone.

## What the business looked like before

Smart Sun Power installs rooftop solar for homes and commercial buildings. A solar sale is not one conversation. It is an enquiry, a call, a site survey, a quotation, often a revised quotation, then procurement, installation, commissioning and payments in stages. Each step involves a different person, and each step can stall.

When we sat down with the sales team, the operations manager and the owner, the same five problems came up again and again.

Leads in three places. Enquiries came through WhatsApp, phone calls and the website, and there was no single list of them.
Follow-ups from memory. No task list, no reminders. If a salesperson forgot, the lead went cold.
Documents everywhere. Survey notes, quotations and customer files were split across chats, email and folders.
Nothing after the sale. Once a deal closed, nobody could easily see where procurement, installation or commissioning stood.
An owner asking around. Pipeline value, conversion and money still owed were only known by asking people.

This is common. WhatsApp is where Indian customers want to talk, so it is where sales start. The trouble is that a chat app is built for conversations, not for a pipeline. You cannot sort it by stage, set a due date on it or see who owns which customer.

## What we built

We did not start from a CRM template. We mapped how a solar job actually moves from first message to final payment, and built the screens around that path.

One record follows the customer from the first enquiry to the last payment. 

## One place for every lead

Leads from the website, calls and WhatsApp referrals land on one dashboard. Each one gets a sales owner and a recorded source, so you can see which channel brings buyers and which brings time-wasters.

## Follow-ups that remind you

The single biggest change for the sales team. 
After each call the salesperson logs what happened and sets the next action. When that action is due, the system alerts them. This sounds small. In practice it was the feature the sales team noticed first, because it took the job of remembering off them.

## Surveys and quotations

Site surveys move from scheduled to completed inside the CRM. Quotation templates fill in the lead and site details automatically and move from draft to final, so nobody retypes a customer’s address or roof size into a new document.

## Installation tracking

When a deal closes, it moves straight into installation, with milestones from material procurement to commissioning. Sales can answer a customer’s “when will it be done?” without calling the site team.

## Payments in stages

Solar jobs are usually paid in parts. The CRM tracks advance, on-installation and on-completion payments, each with a due date, an alert and the receipt linked to it. That is where the 35% improvement in on-time collections came from: overdue amounts are now on a screen instead of in someone’s head.

## A dashboard for the owner

Pipeline value, conversion, sales-cycle length, team performance, profitability and payment status, in real time. The owner no longer has to ask around to know how the month is going.

## Why custom, and not an off-the-shelf CRM?

Off-the-shelf CRMs are good products, and for many businesses they are the right answer. For a solar installer, the gap is everything after the sale. Most general CRMs are built around a deal closing. For Smart Sun Power, closing the deal is roughly the halfway point. Surveys, installation milestones and staged payments are the parts that needed to fit their process, and that is where a generic tool would have needed the most workarounds.

There is also the question of ownership. As with all our projects, the client owns the code and the data. There is no per-user licence that grows as the sales team grows.

## How we got the team to actually use it

A CRM that nobody opens is just a more expensive spreadsheet. We spent as much care on the switch as on the software.

The same work, moved from scattered chats into one connected record. 
Data migration first. Existing leads and customer records were moved into the CRM before anyone switched over, so nothing was lost and nobody had to keep the old spreadsheet open “just in case”.
Hands-on training. Onboarding sessions, written documentation and quick-reference guides for daily tasks.
Support after launch. Fixes, updates and new features based on how the team really used it, not how we guessed they would.

The management team summed it up in the case study: “What used to take three people to coordinate manually is now automated.”

## What we learned

Start from the process, not the features. The most useful screens were the ones that mirrored a step the team already did, such as a survey or a staged payment. We built the steps they had, not the ones a template assumed.

Reminders beat reports. Dashboards are nice for the owner. Day to day, the thing that moved conversion was a salesperson getting an alert at the right moment. If you only build one feature, build that.

Move the data before you move the people. Teams fall back to the old way when the new system feels empty. Migrating the existing records first made the CRM the obvious place to look on day one.

Keep people on the decisions. The CRM reminds, records and totals. It does not decide which customer to chase or what discount to give. That stays with the team, which is also why they trust it.

## Do you need a custom CRM for your small business?

Not always, and we say so on the first call. If you get a handful of enquiries a week and one person handles them, a well-kept spreadsheet with a follow-up date column may be enough for now. If your process is close to a standard sales funnel, an off-the-shelf CRM will probably serve you well.

A custom CRM starts to make sense when:

leads come from several channels and some are clearly being missed;
your work has steps after the sale, such as surveys, installation, delivery or staged payments;
you are paying for workarounds or extra seats to bend a general tool to your process;
you want to own the software and the customer data outright.

If WhatsApp is part of your sales, it can stay that way. The official WhatsApp Business Platform lets a CRM receive and send messages through an approved API, so chats can be logged against a customer rather than lost in a phone. And because a CRM holds personal data, it is worth designing it with India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act in mind from the start: collect what you need, control who can see it and keep it where you can account for it. For solar installers specifically, residential buyers often ask about the PM Surya Ghar rooftop scheme, which is one more reason to keep each customer’s documents and stage in one place.

## Next steps

You can read the full project in our Smart Sun Power case study , see the services we offer , or read why we build in code instead of on automation platforms . If your leads come from more than one list, our post on merging duplicate leads into one master list covers the step before a CRM. When you are ready, tell us how your sales work today and we will tell you honestly whether you need software at all.

## Frequently asked questions
Is a custom CRM worth it for a small business? It is worth it when your process does not fit a standard sales funnel, when leads arrive through several channels and some are missed, or when you need to track work after the sale such as surveys, installation or staged payments. If you only handle a few enquiries a week, a spreadsheet or an off-the-shelf CRM may be enough, and we will tell you so.
Can a CRM work with WhatsApp? Yes. Through the official WhatsApp Business Platform API, a CRM can log incoming messages against the right customer and send approved messages from the CRM. In the solar CRM, WhatsApp referrals land on the same lead dashboard as website and phone enquiries.
How quickly does a CRM show results? For Smart Sun Power, lead conversion rose 28% within three months of go-live and the sales cycle fell from 45 to 28 days. Results depend on how well the CRM fits the process and whether the team uses it daily, which is why data migration and training matter as much as the software.
Will we lose our existing leads when we switch? No. Existing leads and customer records are migrated into the CRM before the team switches over, so nothing is lost and the new system is useful from the first day.
How much does a custom CRM cost? It depends on the number of stages, users and integrations. Groviadigi starts with a free 15-minute call, then a short paid consultancy to map your process, and gives a fixed written quote before any build. Every project includes 3 months of free maintenance, then care plans from ₹5,000 a month.
